Part one

Breakdown: how this video is built

At a glance: picture, packaging, sound

Any short video splits into three layers: the picture, what is laid on top of it (subtitles, styled text, stickers), and the sound. Remake it one layer at a time.

LayerIn this videoHow to make itDetail
Picture (base)live action 14 shotsfilmed in 1 scene“Remake it yourself”
Packaging (on top)text, title, styled text, subtitleadd in the editor: subtitles, styled text and stickers by the timeline“Packaging layer”
Soundvoice（human recording）, 1 sound effectsvoice: record it yourself; effects: add from a library at the listed times“Sound”

Content and structure

  • The whole video's content was not analysed this time (needs AI image reading); subtitle text is under “Packaging layer”
  • No narrative line this time (what each shot is doing in the story needs AI image reading); the “Picture” column of the shot list is a start

Cast, scenes and props

  • No cast extracted this time (needs AI image reading)

Camera and lighting

  • Framing: shot size medium shot 64%, medium close-up 36%; subject is the in-focus region (no face; shot size is an estimate)
  • Camera: moving camera (gimbal / handheld pan) 92%, fixed camera (tripod / mount / on the desk) 8%; typical move pan / track
  • Lighting: soft frontal light (flat light). Key light frontal (from the camera side; both sides of the subject about equally bright), from below (screen / desk bounce / low source); lighting ratio about 1.1:1 (0.2 stops); soft light (wide lit-to-shadow ramp); colour temperature neutral (about 5000K); lower half of the subject is brighter: likely light from below (screen, desk bounce); background slightly soft
  • Grade: natural (close to the original colours); low saturation, normal contrast, normal blacks, overall neutral
  • Format: handheld product shots (unboxing / selling / POV) (face as subject 0%, objects / hands as subject 100%, handheld 92%)

Part two

Remake plan

Remake it yourself: do it in this order

Copy the method and the rhythm, not the pictures: keep what each part does and fill it with your own content and material.

This is a tabletop / unboxing / product. Do the steps in this order; the detail for each is in the matching subsection below.

  1. Write the content: one picture of your own for each of the 14 shots in the shot list
  2. Shoot: phone held vertical, mostly medium shot; light: soft frontal light (flat light) — a large source from the camera side, almost no shadow on the subject: facing a window, a ring light, or a big softbox behind the camera, one large soft light straight above the desk / behind the camera (or two, symmetrical at 45°); grade: natural (close to the original colours) (setups under “Shoot”)
  3. Voice: the original is human recording; record it yourself or use TTS
  4. Edit: follow the order and lengths in the shot list; the original has 14 shots at 1.5s each; 2 transitions under “Edit”
  5. Subtitles and styled text: timing and style under “Packaging layer”
  6. Sound effects: 1; place similar ones from a library at the times under “Sound”
  7. Put it together and compare: hand the shots you made to the agent; it places them on the original timeline, keeps the original where yours are missing, and renders a side-by-side comparison with the original

Shoot

Shoot every shot of one scene before moving to the next; within a scene, shoot the wider sizes first and the close-ups last so the lighting is set only once. Leave about 1s of handle at both ends of every take.

S1: shots #1–#14 (20.7s on screen); Démonstration du blender portable filmée au téléphone dans une cuisine

  • Lighting: backlit / background brighter than subject, key light frame right, three-quarter front, cool (daylight / cool-white LED)
  • Setup medium shot · moving camera (gimbal / handheld pan) · pan / track/pull-out/push-in/static: shots #1, #2, #6, #8–#10, #13, #14, 11.7s on screen, shoot about 27.7s
  • Setup medium shot · fixed camera (tripod / mount / on the desk) · static: shots #11, 1.63s on screen, shoot about 3.6s
  • Setup medium close-up · moving camera (gimbal / handheld pan) · pan / track/push-in/static: shots #3–#5, #7, #12, 7.37s on screen, shoot about 17.4s

Gear (inferred from the measured light):

  • one large soft light straight above the desk / behind the camera (or two, symmetrical at 45°)
  • white desk or white cards to bounce; shadows go lighter

Edit

  • Cut in the order and lengths of the shot list
  • Rhythm: 37.7 cuts per minute, 1.48s average live-action shot; 6 camera set-up(s) / location(s); 1 jump cut(s) and 1 punch-in(s) within the same set-up; inserts (screenshots / screen recordings / cards / stock) take 0%; 62% of cuts land in pauses of the speech (cutting on breaths); transitions cut×11, jump cut×2
